title: Digital Timetable App with Time-Restricted Task Completion Tracking

requirements.text: Implement image upload functionality that accepts timetable images (handwritten or printed) and stores them for processing

quotes: The user will upload an image of their handwritten or printed timetable

acceptanceCriteria: User can select and upload image files from their device
Supported formats include common image types (JPG, PNG)
Upload interface provides visual feedback during upload process

requirements.text: Extract timetable data from uploaded images using OCR, parsing days of the week (Monday-Sunday), time slots, task/subject names, and optional location information, converting to structured JSON format

quotes: The AI must read the image and extract all relevant information such as: Days of the week (Monday, Tuesday, etc.), Time slots for each activity or subject, Subject or activity name, Optional location (if mentioned)

acceptanceCriteria: OCR accurately extracts timetable data from clear images
Handles messy handwriting with reasonable accuracy
Parses time slots in various formats (e.g., '9:00-10:00', '9-10', '09:00 AM - 10:00 AM')
Identifies days of the week correctly
Outputs structured JSON matching the format: {"Monday": [{"time": "9:00-10:00", "subject": "Math", "done": false}]}
Preserves optional location data if present in the image

requirements.text: Display extracted timetable as an editable table with columns for Day, Time, Task/Subject, and Done checkbox, allowing users to modify task names and details

quotes: After extraction, the timetable should be displayed in a user-editable table. Each row must contain: Day, Time slot, Subject or activity, A 'Done' checkbox

acceptanceCriteria: Table displays all extracted timetable entries in rows
Each row shows Day, Time slot, Task/Subject, and Done checkbox
Task/Subject fields are editable by the user
Changes to task names persist and update the underlying data structure
Table is responsive and accessible

requirements.text: Implement time-restricted Done checkbox that only enables during the scheduled time slot for each task, validating current time against task schedule before allowing completion marking

quotes: The 'Done' checkbox should only be enabled if the user is marking the task at the correct scheduled time
If a task is scheduled for 9:00–10:00, the checkbox can only be ticked during this time slot
If the user tries to tick the task before or after the scheduled time, the checkbox should be disabled or restricted

acceptanceCriteria: Done checkbox is disabled when current time is outside the task's scheduled time slot
Done checkbox is enabled only during the exact scheduled time window
Visual indicator shows why checkbox is disabled (e.g., tooltip or message)
System uses accurate current time for validation
Completed tasks remain marked as done after the time window passes
User cannot manually enable or override time restrictions

requirements.text: Store timetable data with task completion status in backend, maintaining synchronization between table display and JSON structure

quotes: The JSON should always match the table
Generate a structured JSON for programmatic use

acceptanceCriteria: Timetable data persists across sessions
Task completion (done) status is stored and retrieved accurately
Updates to task names or details sync to backend immediately
JSON structure matches the specified format with days as keys and arrays of task objects
Data integrity maintained between frontend table and backend JSON

requirements.text: Handle unclear or incomplete timetable images gracefully by leaving blank fields in the JSON structure without crashing, estimating ambiguous time slots when possible and marking them clearly

quotes: If the timetable image is unclear or missing some information: Leave the corresponding fields blank in the JSON or table, Do not crash; maintain the structure
If time slots are ambiguous, estimate them if possible but mark them clearly

acceptanceCriteria: OCR processing never crashes on poor quality images
Missing or unclear fields appear as empty strings or null in JSON
Ambiguous time slots are estimated and flagged with a visual indicator
User can edit fields that were unclear or missing
Error messages inform user if image quality is too poor to extract any data

requirements.text: Provide JSON export functionality that generates downloadable structured JSON of the current timetable matching the displayed table

quotes: The AI should provide both the editable table and structured JSON in one response
Generate a structured JSON for programmatic use

acceptanceCriteria: User can export current timetable as JSON file
Exported JSON matches the exact structure and content displayed in the table
JSON includes all days, time slots, tasks, and completion status
Export is available as a downloadable file

requirements.text: Use the uploaded timetable image (Screenshot_20260223_031932 (1).jpg) as test data for OCR extraction, parsing the daily routine from 8:30 (Wake Up) through 23:00 (Sleep) with tasks like Pharmaceutics, PIC, HAP II, Biochemistry, etc., across all seven days

quotes: The user has uploaded 1 image(s): Screenshot_20260223_031932 (1).jpg

acceptanceCriteria: System successfully extracts all time slots from 8:30 to 23:00

All task names are extracted accurately (Wake Up, Drink Water, Bath/Freshen Up, Pushups + Abs, Breakfast, Pharmaceutics, Cook Healthy Meal, PIC, Lunch, HAP II, Rest, Snack, Biochemistry, Gym/Walk, Dinner, Family/Chat, Night Revision, Sleep)
All seven days (M, T, W, T, F, S, S) are recognized and mapped correctly
Checkbox grid structure is preserved with daily completion tracking

requirements.text: Apply a clean, modern design aesthetic with warm, energetic colors (avoiding blue and purple) featuring clear typography, intuitive table layouts, and visual time indicators that make the timetable inviting and motivating to use daily
acceptanceCriteria: Color scheme uses warm tones (e.g., orange, yellow, green, red accents) appropriate for a daily routine tracker
Typography is clear and readable at various screen sizes
Table layout is intuitive with clear visual hierarchy
Time-based restrictions are communicated through visual cues (color, icons, disabled states)
Overall design feels cohesive and purpose-built for task tracking

constraints: Done checkbox must enforce time restrictions - no manual override allowed
OCR processing must not crash on unclear images - maintain structure integrity
JSON structure must always match table display exactly
All Motoko backend logic must remain in the single main actor file
Do not modify immutable frontend paths (useInternetIdentity.ts, useInternetIdentity.tsx, useActor.ts, main.tsx, components/ui)
nonGoals: Multi-user collaboration or sharing timetables between users
Push notifications or reminders for upcoming tasks
Advanced OCR training or custom handwriting recognition models
Recurring timetable templates or weekly patterns
Task statistics, analytics, or progress tracking over time
